caption_pack_role: Slide 10-14 presenter/manuscript caption source for the premium deck spine.
family_caption: Slides 10-14 form the core result spine: v4 hardening establishes robustness, v2 temporal/RRRM lessons add guardrails, v3 negative results define task limits, v5 biological interpretation turns hits into hypotheses, and v6 human translation keeps translational claims boundary-aware.

slides.title: v4 hardening
slides.headline: Broader grid reduces cherry-pick risk
slides.plain_caption: v4 expands the benchmark across 8 tissues, 8 classifiers, and 4 feature views, while keeping significance boundaries visible.
slides.caption: The v4 hardening layer broadens the benchmark to 256 evaluations across tissue, classifier, and feature-view combinations. It should be read as robustness and coverage evidence, not as a new leaderboard or a claim that every displayed best-row tissue is significant.
slides.claim_boundary: Hardening/coverage evidence only; do not imply every best-row tissue is significant.
slides.do_not_say: Do not imply every best-row tissue is statistically significant.
slides.qa_status: pass: rendered preview, scene plate, and grayscale QA inspected

slides.title: Temporal and RRRM guardrails
slides.headline: Timepoint labels need guardrails
slides.plain_caption: v2 separates preservation effects, descriptive recovery projections, and an underpowered RRRM single-cell pilot before interpretation.
slides.caption: The temporal/RRRM layer shows why timepoint and pilot single-cell labels cannot be over-read: preservation can dominate ISS-T/LAR separation, recovery projections are descriptive, and RRRM composition testing remains underpowered despite benchmark-ready data.
slides.claim_boundary: Preservation and recovery are guardrail lessons; recovery projection is descriptive and RRRM composition tests are underpowered.
slides.do_not_say: Do not present LAR recovery as held-out validation or RRRM composition as mature mechanism.
slides.qa_status: pass: rendered preview and grayscale QA inspected

slides.title: Negative boundary
slides.headline: Negative results set boundaries
slides.plain_caption: v3 makes null and weak-signal settings explicit, including spatial brain and pretrained embedding controls.
slides.caption: The negative-boundary layer frames spatial brain and foundation-model results as useful task limits. The slide supports careful follow-up design, not a universal claim that brain biology is absent or that future spatial or foundation-model analyses must fail.
slides.claim_boundary: Negative result defines current task limits; do not claim universal absence of brain biology or universal foundation-model failure.
slides.do_not_say: Do not claim universal absence of brain spaceflight biology or universal FM failure.
slides.qa_status: pass: rendered preview and grayscale QA inspected after corridor/text revision

slides.title: Biological interpretation
slides.headline: Hits become hypotheses
slides.plain_caption: v5 connects immune shifts, metabolic context, and biomarker triage without making treatment claims.
slides.caption: The biological interpretation layer converts benchmark signals into follow-up hypotheses across immune context, pathway-level metabolism, and target-linked biomarker triage. It is an interpretation layer only, not causal mechanism, clinical validation, or countermeasure recommendation.
slides.claim_boundary: Biological interpretation and target triage only; no causal mechanism, validated countermeasure, or treatment recommendation claim.
slides.do_not_say: Do not call target links treatment recommendations or validated mechanisms.
slides.qa_status: pass: rendered preview and grayscale QA inspected after bubble/path/text revision

slides.title: Human translation boundary
slides.headline: Translation is partial, not direct
slides.plain_caption: v6 shows partial pathway and target-tier alignment while direct gene-level transfer remains weak.
slides.caption: The human-translation layer closes the v1-v7 result core by showing that mouse signals partly carry over at pathway and target-tier levels, while direct gene transfer and TF conservation remain weak. Use it as human-alignment evidence, not clinical proof.
slides.claim_boundary: Partial pathway and target-tier human alignment only; no direct gene-transfer, clinical, or countermeasure claim.
slides.do_not_say: Do not imply clinical validation, direct gene-transfer reliability, or countermeasure actionability.
slides.qa_status: pass: rendered preview and grayscale QA inspected after corridor revision
